In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the net N and P mobilization rates from sediments are not directly related to decomposition rates.
decomposition rates are primarily determined by the amount of organic matter present in the sediment.
the net nutrient mineralization and mobilization from peat sedi-ments are largely controlled by the organic matter quality, but are also strongly dependent on the Fe:PO4 ratio in the pore water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

decomposition, net mineralization rates and mobilization of nutrients are uncoupled and that the internal mobilization of PO(4) is an important source of P to the water layer in non-calcareous fen peat sediments.
net N and P mobilization rates from non-calcareous sediments and floating peat soils are largely determined by their C:P and C: N ratios, and the Fe:PO4 ratios in the pore water.
decomposition and nutrient mineralization rates can be uncoupled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decomposition and nutrient mobilization are not necessarily coupled processes and therefore, nutrient mobilization should be measured in addition to the decomposition rates.
